notes: Run each prompt twice: with /design and as a baseline with no skill. Grade the expectations, then compare screenshots side by side. Visual quality is judged by eye; the checker gives the objective part.

evals.prompt: /design Build a single-file HTML landing page for 'Ledgerline', a bookkeeping app for small cafes. Hero, three things it does, pricing, sign-up.
evals.expected_output: A landing page that looks made for cafe bookkeeping specifically, not a generic SaaS template.
expectations: check-page.mjs exits 0 on the page (no FAIL lines)
check-page.mjs shows no WARN for long-titles, stock-phrases, em-dashes or arrow-links
No purple-to-blue gradient, no emoji icons, no three identical feature cards under a giant hero
Color and type tokens are declared once at the top of the CSS and used throughout
Swap test: with the name 'Ledgerline' hidden, the page still reads as being for cafes (cafe-specific content, terms or visuals)
The reply lists screenshot paths and the checker summary line, and is under 8 lines

evals.prompt: /design Make an admin dashboard page (HTML) for a dog-walking business: today's walks, walkers on shift, late walks, revenue this week.
evals.expected_output: A dense but calm operational dashboard where late walks stand out first.
expectations: check-page.mjs exits 0 and the phone screenshot has no sideways scroll
Late walks are the single most prominent element on first view
Status uses an icon or word plus color, never color alone
Numbers that line up in columns use tabular figures
No all-caps label styles beyond one kind, no decorative 01/02/03 markers

evals.prompt: /design Restyle this settings page to match our brand.
evals.expected_output: The page follows DESIGN.md exactly: brand colors and fonts, no new design system.
expectations: Only colors and fonts from DESIGN.md are used
Every existing field and control from settings.html is still present and works
Reply states which DESIGN.md look was used, in one line
